clue.text: Extreme view about the good old days makes one tense

definitions.text: Extreme view about the good old days
definitions.meaning: a rose-tinted belief that bygone times were flawless, read as a two-word phrase
a verb tense formed with had plus a past participle, as in 'she had gone'

explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link: the first reading is literal (yesterday was flawless), the second is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: The pluperfect is a grammatical tense, and the phrase also literally says the bygone era was flawless.

clue.text: Eat ravenously? Good! Good!

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: Someone cheers a hearty appetite with a double exclamation of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out, or simply to pig, is slang for gorging food greedily.

clue.text: Spanish address? Member of government wastes a little time here

indicators.note: a politician who wastes something loses it, so these letters drop out of the word

parts.note: a senator sits in the upper house of a government
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A politician fritters away a moment here, perhaps on a Spanish trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a link pointing back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish form of address equivalent to Mr or sir.

clue.text: Fuss and bother makes friend swear

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to swear or declare firmly

explanation.surface: A mate who curses causes all sorts of commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is informal for tiresome fuss and protracted bother over something.

clue.text: Talk like an oldie about sixties attire, extremely commonplace

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning
miniskirts, or minis, were the signature fashion of the 1960s

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, so only those two of commonplace are used

explanation.surface: An elderly person chats about the dull clothes of the swinging sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Old people famously reminisce, recalling and talking about their past experiences.

clue.text: Painter dropping odd bits of gear on a site

indicators.note: losing the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and so on of the following words

explanation.surface: An artist leaves bits of his kit lying about on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Like Russia once, treating artists badly

indicators.note: something treated badly is knocked out of shape, so the letters of artists are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old Russia was notorious for mistreating its painters and writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia was ruled by tsars until 1917, so it was tsarist in nature.

clue.text: Food one rescued from flood

definitions.meaning: cured pork from a pig's thigh is a common food
one of Noah's sons, who survived the biblical deluge in the ark

explanation.definitionFit: Ham is cured pork, and also the son of Noah saved from the Flood in Genesis.

clue.text: Star owned boat for smuggling in drug

indicators.note: smuggling slips something inside, so the drug goes into the first word

parts.note: had is the past tense of have, meaning owned
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A celebrity's own yacht is used to run narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the star performer whose name tops the bill.

clue.text: Female below stairs diverts a man naughtily

indicators.note: acting naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters of the three words get rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant girl distracts her male employer in a flirtatious way.
explanation.definitionFit: Below stairs is where domestic staff worked, and a maidservant is a female domestic.

clue.text: Specify one little officer to go back after another, trustworthy type

indicators.note: the reversed part comes after the other officer in the answer

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for general, another officer

indicators.note: going back means running in reverse, so the letters of these two words read right to left

parts.note: to name something is to specify it
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a junior officer

explanation.surface: Military orders: name a junior officer to retreat behind a senior one, a reliable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns NAMELT into TLEMAN, which then follows GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman is a man of honour whose word can be relied upon.

clue.text: Frames for summer's activities?

parts.note: read summer as one who sums, not the season: bead frames used for doing arithmetic

explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame, used by anyone adding up figures, a summer in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: A vehicle attached at the rear of another?

definitions.text: A vehicle attached at the rear of another?

indicators.note: something hitched at the back follows the other piece in the answer

parts.note: a car is another vehicle
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A trailer home being towed behind a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a towed caravan is exactly a vehicle hitched behind another.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed trailer home hitched behind a car.

clue.text: Customer's initial order for piece of furniture offering relaxation

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here of Customer's

parts.note: OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A shopper orders a restful item from a furniture store.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comfortable gives ease and relaxation.

clue.text: Mistake to take little boy such big drinks

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or slip, a mistake
Les is the short form of the boy's name Leslie

explanation.surface: It would be an error to let a small child have such large drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Triples are triple measures of spirits, big drinks at a bar.

clue.text: Bloke giving away tons? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Bloke giving away tons? Yes and no!

indicators.note: something given away is lost, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: Mister is a form of address for any man or bloke

explanation.surface: A man handing out large sums: true in one sense, false in another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no!' is the wit: the wordplay has him give away T, but a tightwad gives nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and is the last man to hand out tons of it.

clue.text: Provinces of avant-garde composer may include popular black music

indicators.note: including something puts it inside, so the music goes within the composer's name

parts.note: Erik Satie was an avant-garde French composer; 'of' him gives the possessive Satie's
rap is a popular music genre originating in Black American culture

explanation.surface: A modernist composer's territories might feature rap.
explanation.definitionFit: Satrapies were the provinces of ancient Persia, each ruled by a satrap.

clue.text: Resent being forced to eat little carrot

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the small word goes into the anagram
something forced is pushed out of shape, so the letters of resent are rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Someone resents being made to eat a small carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrot' reads as a vegetable but means an inducement. 'being forced' gives STENER, which 'to eat' wraps around the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an incentive, as is a sweetener offered to win someone over.

clue.text: Bearing of ship bound for the Antarctic

definitions.meaning: bearing here means putting up with hardship, as in 'beyond bearing'
Shackleton's ship on his 1914 expedition to Antarctica

explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity for bearing hardship, and the name of Shackleton's Antarctic ship.

clue.text: Terribly hot men finish up getting better

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: to end is to finish up

explanation.surface: Feverish men finally start to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the mend is recovering from illness or injury.

clue.text: Clay article — get to collect that

indicators.note: collecting takes something in, so the article goes inside the word for get

parts.note: to earn is to get money
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A pottery item: go and fetch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link pointing back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen means made of baked clay or earth, as in earthenware.

clue.text: Church organisation sends spies around biblical city

indicators.note: the spies go around, so the city is placed inside

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's city in the Bible

explanation.surface: A church body dispatches agents to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the administrative body of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Type that's 100-1 flipping over in race

parts.note: class means type or category

indicators.note: something flipped over is turned the other way, so the two numerals read backwards

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A horse priced at 100-1 that takes a tumble in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Classics are the five major British flat horse races, such as the Derby.

clue.text: Milk dispenser given to man something useful in café

parts.note: a teat dispenses milk, on an animal or a baby's bottle
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A milk jug handed to a man: handy in a café.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tray is used for carrying cups and pots in a café.

clue.text: This person's consumed by desire for a republic

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so this part goes inside the other

parts.note: a yen is a strong desire
this person, the setter, is me; 's is 'is' joining wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being consumed with longing for a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a republic in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Retrieve data on a query book ignored

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter drops from the word

parts.note: a doubt is a query

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch figures about a dubious volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To read out data is to retrieve it from a computer's memory for display.

clue.text: Arab turning up in next to no time

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads letters bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: 'in a mo' is colloquial for in a moment, next to no time

explanation.surface: An Arab arrives almost immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses INAMO. MO is informal British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, an Arab country.

clue.text: Failing to finish, frustrate admiral

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to blight is to frustrate or spoil hopes

explanation.surface: Unfinished business thwarts a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: William Bligh, of the Bounty mutiny, later rose to the rank of vice-admiral.

clue.text: Maths fine? Quite otherwise — one's got bored

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil's maths is fine? Far from it: they're thoroughly bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got bored' means drilled, not weary: a shaft is bored into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine shaft is a vertical tunnel that has been bored or drilled into the earth.

clue.text: Teachers half cut? That's bad!

indicators.note: half of a word is one of its two halves, here the first three letters

parts.note: tutors are teachers

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about teachers being half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is a link: half of the word for teachers is cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is an exclamation of disapproval, as said when something is bad.

clue.text: English script in spaces at the printing house

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a script

explanation.surface: Typing English text into gaps at a print works.
explanation.definitionFit: An em is a unit of space in printing, the width of the letter M.

clue.text: Second print comes out lacking in colour

indicators.note: the letters come out differently, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The reprint of a book emerges looking pale and washed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nondescript means dull and lacking any distinctive character.
